ctx.x: Well, I think he didn't have the success with them because people...Broadway...the promoters forgot that here's a man that wrote a song, 'The Charleston,' that should have endeared him to the entire world, and that anything that he wanted to do, he should have been able to find support.

For example, Dan, I'm in a peculiar position now. I've always been interested in trying to stimulate local interest in activities like Jazz Festival Society in Chicago---in Philadelphia, and I organized the New York Jazz Festival Society here. I haven't done anything important with it. But I think that, why can't mainstreams and guys who know the history of jazz, why can't we begin to build in black communities this kind of thing where incubators are created and out of that can evolve more of the original kind of…
Charlie Parker and he said to me, 'Sam, you just play what you play and I'll play what I play and it'll come out all right.'
